description: Feasibility analysis for NetSquid and QuISP adapters

netsquid.name: NetSquid
netsquid.licence: Free for academic/non-commercial use; requires forum registration. Not on public PyPI; installed from https://pypi.netsquid.org with credentials. Adapter code that imports NetSquid can be distributed, but users need their own NetSquid account to install it.

api.state_formalism: Supports both stabilizer and density-matrix formalisms
api.memory_component: QuantumMemory component with built-in noise models
api.channel_application: Custom models can be attached to components

compatibility.density_matrix: YES — NetSquid supports density-matrix formalism, compatible with WestQuant's Kraus operators
compatibility.erasure_channel: YES — NetSquid can model loss/erasure as a separate outcome
compatibility.event_timing: YES — PyDynAA provides the same event-driven timing as SeQUeNCe
compatibility.noise_double_counting: MUST DISABLE — NetSquid's built-in memory noise models must be disabled to avoid double-counting with WestQuant's channel

adapter_requirements: Create a NetSquid QuantumMemory component that holds the density matrix passively
Attach a custom model that applies the WestQuant channel at retrieval time
Disable all built-in noise models (T1, T2, dephasing)
Use PyDynAA's event scheduler for timing
Feed the same pre-generated random trace as SeQUeNCe and QuNetSim
netsquid.feasibility: HIGH — NetSquid's density-matrix formalism and component architecture are directly compatible with WestQuant's channel model. The main work is creating a custom memory component and disabling built-in noise.
blockers: NetSquid is not on public PyPI — users need a forum account
Cannot be tested in CI without credentials
netsquid.estimated_effort: 2-3 days for a minimal adapter; 1 week for full benchmark integration

quisp.name: QuISP

api.state_formalism: Primarily error-basis (stabilizer-like); density-matrix mode exists but is limited to ~56 qubits
api.memory_component: QNIC (Quantum Network Interface Card) with per-qubit memory
api.channel_application: Error models attached to channels and components

compatibility.density_matrix: PARTIAL — QuISP can output density matrices but primarily operates in the error basis. The WestQuant channel's Kraus operators would need to be translated to QuISP's error model.
compatibility.erasure_channel: PARTIAL — QuISP supports non-Pauli errors including loss, but the erasure channel's 3-outcome measurement may not map cleanly to QuISP's error tracking.
compatibility.noise_double_counting: MUST DISABLE — QuISP's built-in error models must be disabled or set to zero

adapter_requirements: Build QuISP from source with OMNeT++ and Eigen
Create a custom QuISP module that applies the WestQuant channel
Translate Kraus operators to QuISP's error-basis representation
Or: use QuISP's density-matrix mode (limited to small systems)
quisp.feasibility: MEDIUM — QuISP's error-basis formalism is not directly compatible with WestQuant's density-matrix channel. A density-matrix mode exists but is limited. The adapter would need either a formalism translation layer or a restriction to density-matrix mode.
blockers: QuISP requires OMNeT++ (C++ framework) — heavy dependency
Error-basis formalism may not support general CPTP maps
Installation is complex (OMNeT++ + Eigen + QuISP build)
Python API is limited — QuISP is primarily C++
quisp.estimated_effort: 1-2 weeks for a minimal adapter; 3-4 weeks for full benchmark integration

recommendation.rationale: NetSquid's density-matrix formalism is directly compatible with WestQuant's channel model. QuISP's error-basis formalism requires a translation layer that may not preserve the channel's full physics. NetSquid also has a Python API, while QuISP is primarily C++.
next_steps: 1. Register for a NetSquid forum account
2. Install NetSquid in a test environment
3. Prototype a minimal adapter that creates a passive memory and applies a channel
4. Run the existing benchmark config with the NetSquid adapter
5. Compare results against SeQUeNCe and QuNetSim
6. For QuISP: evaluate whether the density-matrix mode supports the erasure channel
7. If yes, prototype a QuISP adapter; if no, defer QuISP to a future release

netsquid.note: Users must have a NetSquid forum account to install NetSquid itself

quisp.install_command: Not available via pip — build from source
quisp.note: QuISP requires OMNeT++ and Eigen; not pip-installable
